modules.what_to_extract: Refactor the 5 execute_* methods into a shared _execute_with_envelope(tool_name, runner_fn, mutation=False) template to eliminate duplicated gating logic. Extract _claim_mutation_lease + _release_mutation_lease into lease_gate.py. Extract _to_execution_result status mapping into result_builder.py. modules.risk: medium — execute_* methods follow a well-defined pattern making template extraction mechanical. The lease gate touches coordination store (mutation gating) — must preserve fail-closed behavior (store errors block mutation, not allow it). _to_execution_result status mapping is pure logic extraction
modules.test_impact: 8-12 tests — template gating tests, lease gate tests, result builder tests, dispatch map tests
modules.notes: The 5 execute_* methods share a 6-step pattern: (1) validate tool_name, (2) adapter.prepare(), (3) check BLOCKED/REFUSED status, (4) validate envelope schema, (5) claim lease if mutation, (6) execute tool. Steps 1-4 are identical across all 5 methods. Extracting them into a shared _execute_with_envelope would reduce ~200 lines of duplicate gating. The lease gate extraction is moderate risk because coordination_enabled=False must still skip lease acquisition — backward compat is required.

cross_cutting_opportunities.name: Shared process lifecycle management
cross_cutting_opportunities.description: bridge_server.py (_kill_process with SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation), server_lifecycle_executor.py (_kill_process with SIGTERM/SIGKILL), and fleet_controller.py (stop_instance with SIGTERM/SIGKILL) all implement process lifecycle with signal management. A shared _process_controller.py could eliminate ~60 lines of duplicated signal handling across 3 modules.

cross_cutting_opportunities.name: Mode-dispatcher pattern in compiler.py mirrors tool-dispatcher in tool_invocation_execution.py
cross_cutting_opportunities.description: compiler.py's execute() function dispatches 5 context modes via if/elif chains. tool_invocation_execution.py's execute_runtime_exec dispatches 4 sub-tools via if/elif chains. Both could use a registry/map pattern for mode→handler dispatch. Centralizing the dispatch pattern could inform a future ContextDispatcher abstraction.

cross_cutting_opportunities.name: Health polling blocking pattern
cross_cutting_opportunities.description: server_lifecycle_executor.py uses time.sleep(2) in a sync while-loop for health polling. bridge_server.py has probe methods that are async. fleet_controller.py uses time.sleep(0.5) and subprocess.poll(). All three could benefit from a shared async health polling utility with configurable timeouts.
